title: low-and-slow smoked russian pork pilaf
description: a savory, smoky pilaf dish featuring pork, mirin, and a hint of Russian flavor. This dish is perfect for a weeknight dinner.
instructions: Season the pork shoulder with smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork shoulder until browned on all sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the pork shoulder to the smoker and cook for 4-5 hours, or until tender and easily shredded with a fork.
While the pork is cooking, heat the chicken broth and apple cider vinegar in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion to the saucepan and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the uncooked rice to the saucepan and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Transfer the rice mixture to the smoker with the pork and cook for an additional 30-40 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Shred the pork with two forks and stir into the rice mixture.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.
